new_entities.name: Hydrocortisone replacement in chronic Addison's disease
aliases: hydrocortisone for chronic primary adrenal insufficiency
new_entities.description: Chronic oral hydrocortisone replacement, including dose and formulation strategies, used to treat primary adrenal insufficiency.

new_entities.name: Quality of life
new_entities.description: Health-related quality of life measured with generic or disease-specific instruments.

edges.effect_quant: Hydrocortisone replacement strategy can shift quality-of-life outcomes in chronic adrenal insufficiency, but the signal is formulation- and dose-dependent rather than uniformly restorative. In a 47-patient randomized trial, higher replacement doses improved several depression, fatigue, pain, and RAND-36 domains versus lower doses, while a 64-patient regimen trial found the effect of dose timing on HRQoL inconclusive; newer dual-release studies suggest modest psychological benefit without full normalization of well-being.
edges.population: adults with chronic primary adrenal insufficiency, mainly Addison's disease, treated with oral hydrocortisone replacement regimens
edges.mechanism: More physiologic cortisol exposure may reduce under-replacement symptoms such as fatigue, low vitality, pain, and depressive symptom burden, but both under-replacement and overtreatment can impair well-being.
edges.summary: This is a genuinely mixed edge. Hydrocortisone is essential and some dosing or formulation strategies improve specific quality-of-life domains, but standard replacement does not reliably normalize well-being and the gains are usually modest rather than transformative.
edges.caveats: The evidence mixes primary and secondary adrenal insufficiency and compares both dose and formulation strategies rather than placebo versus no treatment. Better symptoms at higher dose can also reflect short-term trade-offs that are not equivalent to an endorsement of chronic over-replacement.

evidence.citation: Tiemensma J et al 2014 Clin Endocrinol (Oxf)
evidence.notes: A randomized, double-blind, crossover study comparing two- and four-dose hydrocortisone regimen with regard to quality of life, cortisol and ACTH profiles in patients with primary adrenal insufficiency.
Hydrocortisone Dose Influences Pain, Depressive Symptoms and Perceived Health in Adrenal Insufficiency: A Randomized Controlled Trial.

evidence.citation: Dineen R et al 2021 Eur J Endocrinol
evidence.notes: Cardiometabolic and psychological effects of dual-release hydrocortisone: a cross-over study.
